title: Trace & Cost Playbook — Observability Notes (week of Mar 16 2026)
content:
Purpose: working notes for the observability team this week. Focus: tracing sample policy tweaks, dashboard compact redesign, and validating cost telemetry alerts driven by token-volume spikes. This is a working doc (notes + decisions + actions) — not final runbook yet.

Attendees (standup rotation): Aisha (owner), Tom, Ruth, Omar, Leah, + SRE on-call (Priya joining for incident sync).

Quick TL;DR:
- Root cause hypothesis for 2026-03-15 tail-latency spike: inefficient cross-service fanout from the inference gateway when a small percentage of requests hit long-context paths (client B).
- Immediate mitigation: reduce sampling weight for gateway->microservice children traces to 10% for non-production, increase priority sampling for error traces and >1s spans. Rolling now (OBS-1102).
- Dashboard work: compact 'cost telemetry' panel to surface per-model token cost hotpaths (PR 482). Prototype in staging Grafana; needs UX tweaks and a perf test.
- Action items assigned below (owners + due dates).

Notes / Investigation details:
1) Tracing & Sampling
- Evidence: Tempo traces show repeated patterns where gateway forks 4 downstream requests; 2 downstream services are quick, 2 are slow (KV-cache misses). When gateway parallelism spikes, the slow tail inflates p99.
- Sampling currently set to head-based 5% + 100% for error traces. That leaves many long tails unobserved. We need targeted tail sampling.
- Proposed sampling policy (short-term):
  - Keep head-based baseline: 5%
  - If span duration > 500ms OR span has attribute 'kv.cache_miss' OR http.status >= 500 => force-sample (100%)
  - Gateway fanout child spans: reduce deterministic sampling to 10% to lower ingestion cost
  - Add a reservoir sampler for p99 candidates: keep ~1k traces/day chosen by a rolling scoring function (duration * error_flag * frequency).
- Implementation notes: Tom will update the sampling config in the agent repo (PR OBS-1102) and test in staging (deadline 2026-03-19).
- Unresolved: need to confirm whether forcing on 'kv.cache_miss' attribute will generate too many traces for customers with high cache-miss rates. Ruth to run a 48h sample on prod traffic to estimate volume (OBS-1103).

2) Dashboards & Alerts
- Cost telemetry dashboard: goal is actionable triage — show per-model token-rate, estimated $/minute, and top 5 endpoints by cost delta. Current dashboards are too wide and double-count cached tokens.
- PR 482 introduces a compact panel set and a corrected token-rate query (exclude cached responses using trace attribute token_cache_status=\"HIT\").
- UX asks: Leah to prototype a narrow layout for mobile/console embedding and add a hover tooltip with “how cost is computed”. UX mock due 2026-03-20.
- Alerts: reduce noisy cost alerts by switching from static thresholds to a baseline + deviation formula (baseline = 7d median, alert if > 3x IQR and > $50/day). Omar to implement in Alertmanager rule (due 2026-03-22).

3) Cost Telemetry Accuracy
- Problem spotted: some short-lived test jobs were skewing the cost dashboard because we were attributing GPU warmup tokens to model inference. Fix: exclude jobs with label job_type=\"benchmark\" at query time (quick filter). Applied in staging; monitor effect for 24h.
- Question: do we need a separate “warmup” token bucket in billing estimates? Product asked for guidance. Decision deferred to product sync next week.

4) Incident retrospective (mini): March 15 tail-latency spike
- Timeline: 13:05 spike (p99 from 420ms -> 1.8s), error rate unchanged. 13:07 alerted by SRE. 13:12 traced to gateway fanout pattern and a sudden drop in local KV cache hit-rate caused by a TTL sweep from a user job.
- Mitigation applied: increased gateway retry budget and pinned tolerant fallback model for a short period (reduced p99 to 620ms by 13:30).
- Follow-ups: implement TTL-sweep detection in telemetry (Ruth), and add automated temporary fallback (Aisha) to flip to smaller model if aggregate queue depth > threshold.

Action items (owner — due):
- Tom Nguyen — update agent sampling config (PR OBS-1102), run staging test, and note ingestion delta (due 2026-03-19).
- Ruth Garcia — run 48h prod sample to estimate traces forced by 'kv.cache_miss' rule and produce numbers for next sync (JIRA-OBS-1103) (due 2026-03-20).
- Omar Hassan — convert cost alerts from static threshold -> baseline+deviation rules in Alertmanager; add suppression window for known weekly benchmarks (due 2026-03-22).
- Leah Kim — design compact dashboard layout + tooltip copy; prepare screenshot for exec review (due 2026-03-20).
- Aisha Patel — draft fallback playbook (criteria, runbook steps) and link to runbooks/SRE on-call guide (due 2026-03-24).

Short-term experiments to run (tracking):
- Experiment A: reservoir sampling set at 1k/day vs 5k/day for 7 days — measure p99 detection rate vs ingestion cost. Metric owner: Tom.
- Experiment B: token attribution fix for cached tokens (staging -> canary) — measure delta in reported cost for top 10 customers. Metric owner: Omar.

Links / refs to check before next sync:
- Confluence: Trace Sampling Playbook (link above) — update with our sample config if approved.
- Slack thread: #observability-incidents (look for thread ts: 1710804000.000200) — includes raw trace IDs.
- GitHub: observability PR 482 (dashboard compact) — review comments on query correctness.
- JIRA: OBS-1102 sampling config / OBS-1103 sampling volume analysis.

Open questions / discussion items for next weekly sync:
- Is forcing on 'kv.cache_miss' a sustainable policy, or will it bias retention cost too high for customers with noisy caches?
- Should we surface a per-customer estimated cost impact when deciding to force-sample traced events? (privacy/ops tradeoff)
- Product question: warmup token accounting — billable or not? If not, how to detect reliably across deployments?

Misc / notes to self:
- Put a reminder to run the ingestion cost delta script after Tom's PR merges (script: scripts/estimate_ingestion_delta.sh).
- Check with legal if linked_artifacts that expose raw trace IDs are allowed in Confluence pages.

Next sync: 2026-03-23 10:00am PT (observability weekly). Focus: sampling results, dashboard QA, and cost alert false-positive rate.

End of notes.
